# Bullets from the players ship should always fall on the beat

## Problem statement

Player auto-fire currently uses per-weapon cooldowns started at collection time (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, `Player.tryFire`), so shots drift relative to any musical pulse and different active weapons fire out of phase. Make every player shot land on a shared musical grid: player fire is globally quantised to an **80 BPM** beat, and every weapon's fire rate is an exact subdivision of that beat. The values are configurable rather than hard-coded.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the ship's shots to feel rhythmically locked to a consistent 80 BPM pulse, so the auto-fire has a musical cadence even with no background music.
- **AI agents / developers** — need a single, pure beat-clock module and a catalogue-wide invariant so any current or future weapon (e.g. the planned 20 BPM quarter-time large/explosive bullet) can be added without accidentally firing off the beat.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my ship's bullets to leave on the beat, so the auto-fire feels deliberate and rhythmic rather than mechanically drifting.
- As a **player**, I want every weapon I collect to keep firing in time with the same beat, so switching weapons never makes the rhythm stumble.
- As a **developer**, I want a weapon's fire rate to be expressed as a subdivision of the beat and validated by a test, so I cannot add an off-grid weapon by mistake.
- As a **developer**, I want the BPM and per-weapon subdivisions to be configurable, so the feel can be tuned (and tested) without editing hard-coded literals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock.** A new pure, unit-testable module (e.g. `src/utils/beat.ts`) derives the beat period from a **configurable** BPM (default **80 BPM** → 750 ms/beat), tracks a beat anchor/time origin, and exposes a quantisation helper that maps an arbitrary elapsed time to the next beat/subdivision tick (`nextTick(t)`, `isOnBeat/fireTimeFor(interval, t)`, etc.). No `Date`/frame coupling; deterministic given an input time.
- [ ] **AC2 — All player fire is globally quantised.** Player auto-fire (`Player.tryFire` and its callers in `CombatScene`/`GymWeapons`) emits shots only on ticks of the shared beat clock, phase-locked to the scene/beat anchor — never off-grid — regardless of when a weapon is collected or the frame rate. All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns). Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick.
- [ ] **AC3 — Per-weapon subdivisions + catalogue-wide invariant.** Each weapon's fire interval is an exact subdivision of the beat: **cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat)**, **spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat)**. A catalogue-wide test asserts every `WeaponDefinition.fireRateMs` satisfies `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` (equivalently `fireRateMs × n === beatPeriodMs` for a positive integer `n`), so the future 20 BPM quarter-time weapon and any other new weapon are on-grid by construction.
- [ ] **AC4 — All values configurable.** BPM, the per-weapon subdivisions/fire rates, and the quantisation behaviour are configurable through the project's existing config plumbing (`src/core/rules.ts` and/or `src/core/config.ts`/`constants.ts`; persisted where the existing pattern persists), with sane defaults — no scattered hard-coded beat/rate literals. Tests assert a config override changes the firing cadence.
- [ ] **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover the beat module (period from BPM, quantisation boundaries/edge cases, config override), the catalogue invariant (AC3), and `Player.tryFire`/auto-fire emitting only on grid ticks with multiple active weapons phase-locked. Scene-level tests (gameHarness) assert real bullet spawns land on grid ticks across multiple frames and are framerate-independent. All tests serve a distinct behaviour.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries — in particular GDD §2.3/§4.4 (the "Cannon fires every ~400 ms" wording and the weapon fire-rate description) and any beat/config tuning docs.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). No external art/audio assets.
- **Silent timing grid only:** per producer, the beat is an internal scheduling contract — **no audible metronome and no background music** (GDD §7.3/§8 keep music out of MVP scope). No beat audio/visual indicator is in scope.
- **Player bullets only:** enemy fire timing is unchanged (the item is titled "from the players ship").
- **Scope:** applies to all scenes that auto-fire the player (PlayScene via `CombatScene`, and the gym scenes reusing `Player`), through one shared beat module — not per-scene duplicates.
- **Beat anchor:** the beat clock is anchored at scene/player start and advances with game time (pauses with the game if paused).
- **No behaviour change beyond timing:** weapon patterns, bullet visuals, lifetimes, cumulative+timed semantics and Reset behaviour are unchanged; only fire timing changes.

## Existing state

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` defines `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` with hard-coded `fireRateMs` (cannon 400, spread 600, dual 500, rapid 125) and `bulletLifetime` values; heading/pattern math is pure.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` holds per-weapon cooldowns in `_weaponCooldowns` and `tryFire(dt)` re-arms a fired weapon's cooldown to its own `fireRateMs` (independent timers, phase set by collection time). Cumulative + timed semantics (`equipWeapon`, `resetWeapon`, `tickWeaponTimers`) are implemented and tested.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (`_autoFire`) and `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` (`_autoFire`) call `player.tryFire(dt)` each frame and spawn bullets via `createBulletsFromHeading`/`angleToVelocity`.
- **No beat/BPM/clock infrastructure exists anywhere in `src/`**; there is no music system (GDD §7.3 out-of-MVP).
- Config precedent: `src/core/rules.ts` (localStorage-persisted `GameRules`, e.g. power-up spawn interval) and `src/core/config.ts`/`configTypes.ts` (CSV-backed ship config). `src/core/constants.ts` holds `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` etc.
- Related completed work: AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR (weapon catalogue + auto-fire), AH-0MUD9R3070063DDR (`tryFire` extraction), AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6 (cumulative/timed weapons), AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0 (bullet lifetimes).

## Desired change

1. Add a pure **beat module** (`src/utils/beat.ts`): BPM → beat period, beat anchor, and quantisation helpers (`nextSubdivisionTick`, `shotTimeFor`, `isOnGrid`). Configurable BPM (default 80).
2. Re-express each `WeaponDefinition` fire rate as a **beat subdivision** (cannon 2/beat, spread 1/beat, dual 1/beat, rapid 6/beat) derived from the beat period; add the catalogue-wide on-grid invariant test.
3. Replace per-weapon free-running cooldowns in `Player.tryFire` with **phase-locked scheduling**: a weapon's next shot time is the smallest multiple of its interval at/after the current beat-clock time (anchored at the shared beat origin), so every shot lands on a grid tick and active weapons stay in phase. Collection may delay the first shot to the next grid tick (by design).
4. Wire the shared beat clock into `CombatScene._autoFire` and `GymWeapons._autoFire` (and any other `Player.tryFire` callers) so the scene supplies/uses the same clock.
5. Make BPM and the per-weapon subdivisions **configurable** through the existing config plumbing with defaults, rather than literals.
6. Update unit + scene-harness tests (existing `weapons.test.ts`, `Player.test.ts`, `GymWeapons.test.ts`, `CombatScene` tests) and documentation (GDD §2.3/§4.4, README).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/beat.ts` — **NEW** — pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock + quantisation helpers.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — fire rates re-expressed as beat subdivisions; catalogue-wide on-grid invariant.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `tryFire`/cooldown model → phase-locked scheduling on the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_autoFire` drives the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — `_autoFire` drives the shared beat clock.
- `src/core/rules.ts` / `src/core/config.ts` (and/or `src/core/constants.ts`) — configurable BPM + per-weapon subdivisions with defaults.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts`, **NEW** `src/utils/beat.test.ts`, `src/entities/Player.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` — coverage for quantisation, invariant and scene emission.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.3/§4.4; `README.md` — document the beat-aligned fire model.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Gameplay-feel change:** current rates (cannon 400 → 375 ms; spread 600 → 750 ms; dual 500 → 750 ms; rapid 125 unchanged) slightly change DPS/cadence, and collection now delays the first shot to the next grid tick. Assumption: acceptable and intended ("must always fall on the beat").
- **Definition of "the beat" without music:** resolved by the producer — silent internal grid; no audible/visual reference. The beat is only observable through bullet cadence and tests.
- **Config surface choice:** the producer requires configurability, but the exact home (localStorage rules vs CSV ship config vs constants) is a planning decision; the ACs require at least one tested override path.
- **Phase-locking and multiple weapons:** cumulative weapons with different subdivisions must share the anchor; an implementation that keeps independent cooldowns will drift — the AC2 test guards this.
- **Frame quantisation edge cases:** shots must be attributed to the correct grid tick under variable `dt` (including large deltas), and remain framerate-independent — explicit boundary tests required.
- **Scope-creep risk:** audible beat/music, enemy fire quantisation, and beat-synced visuals are out of scope; record as linked work items rather than folding in.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** (completed) — "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene": origin of `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, the fire-rate constants and `Player` auto-fire this item re-times.
- **AH-0MUD9R3070063DDR** (completed) — "Extract auto-fire with onWeaponFired hook": the `tryFire` auto-fire architecture being changed.
- **AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6** (completed) — "Make weapons both cumalative and time out": cumulative per-weapon timers/cooldowns.
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** (completed) — "Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen": per-weapon bullet lifetimes adjacent to the fire-rate config.
- **AH-0MTGS8TWU006WTFX** (completed) — "Wire shoot audio into GymWeapons._autoFire()": fire cues whose cadence follows the fire rate.
- **AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1** (completed) — "Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD": the audio-scope boundary (no music).
- **GDD (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — §2.3 auto-fire (~400 ms wording), §4.4 weapon fire rates/lifetimes, §7.3 audio (music out of scope), §8 future scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Beat semantics — (a) per-weapon beat-subdivision intervals with independent cooldowns, or (b) a single 80 BPM clock with every shot snapped to the next grid tick?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **(b) global beat quantisation**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "What is the beat reference — (a) silent internal grid only, (b) audible metronome, or (c) visual beat indicator?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **(a) silent internal grid only** (no music; consistent with GDD §7.3). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Per-weapon subdivisions and the catalogue-wide invariant?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **as recommended** — cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat), spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat), dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat), rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat); invariant `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` enforced for the whole catalogue. Source: interactive reply.
- Producer note (interactive, given alongside the answers to Q1–Q3): **all values must be configurable** (BPM, per-weapon subdivisions, quantisation behaviour). Source: interactive reply.

> Prior answers changed: none — all answers above are the final accepted versions.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** – Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen (completed)
- **AH-0MUFGUR9C003XD77** – GitHub Pages deploy rejects release tags (environment policy allows only dev) (in-progress)
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ** – Gym index scene (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: add, always, assert, based, beat (+30 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: add, always, based, beat, bullet (+29 more)

**Phase 3 — Emission + wiring**

**Phase 4 — Verification + handoff**

# Intake Brief: Divers should not return (AH-0MUAYB957002EMYV)

## Headline

While a Diver is away from the formation on its dive attack, the whole enemy cluster must hold its current position (freeze its drift) and resume only once every Diver has rejoined; the Diver still returns, but to its slot in the *current* formation and never to the stale dive-start point.

## Problem statement

Divers dive out of formation toward the player, pause, then glide back to a formation that has kept drifting in the meantime. This reads as the Diver "chasing" a moving cluster and makes the return feel disconnected from the attack. The cluster should instead stop moving while a Diver is away, so the attack reads as: the formation holds, the Diver dives, pauses and rejoins the same (stationary) formation, and only then does the cluster continue on its way.

## Users

- **Player:** Reads the dive attack as deliberate — the formation hesitates, the Diver commits, and the Diver visibly re-forms with its group rather than chasing it.
- **Developer:** Gets a small, explicit "hold the formation" seam shared by the gym base scene and `PlayScene`, with deterministic tests.

Example user stories:

- *As a player, when a Diver dives at me the rest of its cluster stays put until the Diver has rejoined, so I can read where the formation is and plan my movement.*
- *As a developer, I want a single optional entity seam that tells a formation scene "hold the cluster this frame", so the gym and the shipped game cannot diverge.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — The formation holds while a Diver is away.** While any Diver is in a non-`FORMATION` state (`DIVING`, `PAUSING` or `RETURNING`), the formation base does not advance: `GymFormationScene.tick()` leaves `formationBaseX` unchanged (and does not fire the wrap/respawn), and `PlayScene._moveEnemies()` leaves `driftX`/`driftDir` unchanged. *Verification:* deterministic tests in `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` and `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` assert the base/drift is unchanged after ticks with a Diver in each non-formation state, and unchanged while a second Diver is still holding; a destroyed Diver (`alive === false`) in a non-`FORMATION` state must NOT hold the formation, so the gate must consider only living entities and a mid-dive kill cannot freeze the cluster forever.
2. **AC2 — The formation resumes once every Diver has rejoined.** As soon as no Diver is detached (all in `FORMATION`), the formation resumes moving from the frozen position with no jump/snap. *Verification:* a two-diver test asserts the formation stays frozen while one is away and continues from exactly the held `formationBaseX`/`driftX` once both are back.
3. **AC3 — Divers return to their slot in the current formation.** `Diver._handleReturn()` continues to glide onto the slot evaluated live from the formation base (`baseX + col * spacingX`, `baseY + row * spacingY`) and never to a stale dive-start coordinate; a returning Diver never relocates the cluster to meet it. *Verification:* a unit test asserts the return target re-evaluates the supplied base each frame; the existing smooth-return / no-jump tests (`AH-0MTCP1CKB00480BD`, `AH-0MTEI361E000IXYB`) stay green.
4. **AC4 — Dive/return geometry and existing behaviour preserved.** The diagonal bezier dive toward the snapshotted player position, the 500 ms pause, the ~3 s hold, spread-shot firing, dive/pause/return rotation, audio and explosion behaviour are all unchanged, and non-Diver entities (Scout/Tank/Phaser/Swarm/Asteroid/Boss) behave exactly as before. *Verification:* the existing `Diver.test.ts` suites pass unmodified, and a scene test confirms a formation with no Diver still drifts.
5. **AC5 — Tests, docs and full suite.** New deterministic tests cover the hold seam and freeze/resume in both scenes; all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (notably `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` and GDD §4.1 E2); the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Shared seam, both scenes.** Add an optional entity method (working name `requiresFormationHold?(): boolean`) to `FormationSceneEntity` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`) **and** to the shared `EnemyEntity` seam in `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` (alongside `DestructionAudioSeam`), so `PlayScene` can query it on the union type. Non-Diver entities omit it; call sites use optional chaining.
- **Two drift implementations must both be gated.** `GymFormationScene.tick()` (`formationBaseX`, rightward drift + wrap) and `PlayScene._moveEnemies()` (`driftX`/`driftDir`, ping-pong drift) are independent and must each consult the seam.
- **Keep the diagonal dive (Q3-A).** Do not change the dive shape, and do not fold in the open docs item `AH-0MUEI8HSU000QLEA` (GDD calls the dive vertical while the code is diagonal) — that stays a separate item.
- **No new audio/VFX and no timing/config-default changes.** Use the existing `DIVER_*` constants.
- **Freeze scope.** The hold applies for the entire detached window (`DIVING`, `PAUSING`, `RETURNING`); the formation must not wrap/respawn during a hold.
- **Out of scope:** closing formation gaps / restructuring the cluster's internal layout (`Q2-C`) and preventing wrap-only relocation (`Q2-D`) were not selected.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Diver.ts` runs a four-state machine (`FORMATION → DIVING → PAUSING → RETURNING → FORMATION`). The dive is a diagonal quadratic bezier from the formation slot to the player position snapshotted at dive start (`AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX`); the pause is 500 ms (`AH-0MU0EIDQQ003S1JT`); `_handleReturn()` glides from the dive target onto the slot evaluated each frame from the live `baseX`/`baseY` (`AH-0MTEI361E000IXYB`), so it already rejoins the drifting cluster without a snap.
- The formation base is advanced unconditionally: `GymFormationScene.tick()` does `formationBaseX += config.driftSpeed * dt` then wraps when it exceeds `GAME_WIDTH + 60`; `PlayScene._moveEnemies()` advances `driftX` with a `driftDir` ping-pong bounded by `FORMATION_DRIFT_RANGE`. Neither consults entity state.
- There is no seam today by which an entity can ask its scene to hold the formation.
- Open `AH-0MUEI8HSU000QLEA` records that GDD §4.1 still describes a vertical/x-locked dive while the implementation is diagonal (pre-existing, not caused by this item).

## Desired change

1. Give the `Diver` a way to report that it is detached from the formation (working name `requiresFormationHold()` returning `this._state !== DiverState.FORMATION`), published through the shared entity seam so both scenes can query it.
2. Gate the drift advance (and, in the gym scene, the wrap/respawn) on **no** entity requiring a hold. While held, the base stays fixed; every entity's `applyFormationPosition` still runs each frame with the unchanged base so the Diver can rejoin precisely.
3. Resume normal drift automatically on the first frame after the last detached Diver re-enters `FORMATION`.
4. **Hold only on living entities.** The two scene gates must ignore destroyed Divers: a Diver killed mid-`DIVING`/`PAUSING`/`RETURNING` must stop holding immediately so a dead Diver can never freeze the cluster. Implement the seam as `this.alive && this._state !== DiverState.FORMATION` (or filter `entity.alive` at both call sites) and cover it with a test.

Implementation order (test-first): (1) add the failing tests — the seam unit test in `Diver.test.ts` and the freeze/resume scene tests (single diver, two divers, destroyed diver, and no-Diver-still-drifts); (2) add the optional seam to `Diver` and to both entity interfaces (`FormationSceneEntity`, `EnemyEntity`); (3) gate the two drift sites; (4) run the full suite and update the docs (AC5).

No change is required to the Diver's return target logic — with the cluster frozen, the "current" slot is stationary, so the Diver lands exactly where it left.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — implement the `requiresFormationHold()` seam (true for `DIVING`/`PAUSING`/`RETURNING`); class JSDoc note on the hold behaviour.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — add the optional seam to `FormationSceneEntity`; gate the `formationBaseX` advance + respawn in `tick()` on no entity holding.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — gate `driftX`/`driftDir` advance in `_moveEnemies()` on no entity holding.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — extend the shared `EnemyEntity` seam with the optional `requiresFormationHold` method.
- `src/entities/Diver.test.ts` — seam unit tests (state → hold true/false across the cycle).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — freeze/resume integration tests (single and multiple divers; non-Diver formation still drifts; respawn suppressed during a hold).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — `_moveEnemies` freeze/resume test (ping-pong drift preserved).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — document the formation hold and update the E2/behaviour tables.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — GDD §4.1 E2: note that the cluster holds while a Diver is away.

## Related work

- `AH-0MU0EIDQQ003S1JT` — *Diver should pause before returning* (completed): introduced `DiverState.PAUSING` with a configurable 500 ms pause. This item extends the attack window that now holds the formation.
- `AH-0MTEI361E000IXYB` — *Fix Diver.ts: lock x during dive and smooth return to current formation slot* (completed) and `AH-0MTCP1CKB00480BD` — *Diver jumps on return from dive* (completed): established the smooth return onto the *current* slot, which AC3 preserves.
- `AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX` — *Diver should rotate to face the player and dive towards them* (completed): made the dive diagonal and player-targeted; preserved by AC4/Q3-A.
- `AH-0MUEI8HSU000QLEA` — *Diver docs stale: dive described as x-locked but implemented as diagonal* (open): related documentation discrepancy, explicitly **not** folded into this item.
- `AH-0MTFTIZX7005DNFW` — *GymDiver AC1 … wall-clock flaky under full-suite parallel load* (completed): determinism precedent for the new tests (tick-driven, no wall-clock).
- `AH-0MTPLHLZ3006MOC4` — *Stale formation entities crash on GymEnemies scene restart* (completed): the `_localPhase`/no-`scene`-deref constraint that the seam must respect (no new `scene` dereference in the Diver).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (documented, Q2-B):** `PAUSING` counts as "away", so the freeze covers all non-`FORMATION` states. This keeps the cluster stationary for the entire attack rather than twitching during the 500 ms pause.
- **Risk — long freezes when divers are desynchronised.** All divers share the same hold timer, so they normally dive together and the cluster freezes for the attack window (~3.3 s of a ~6.3 s cycle). If divers become desynchronised (destruction and later respawn), the cluster could be held for extended periods. Mitigation: the hold is released as soon as no diver is detached; monitor during playtest and tune the hold timing if it reads poorly.
- **Risk — ping-pong drift state.** In `PlayScene` the freeze must not corrupt `driftDir`; the resume test must assert direction continuity.
- **Risk — destroyed divers.** A Diver destroyed mid-dive/return must stop holding the formation (its `alive` flag is false / it is removed). Add a test so a dead Diver cannot freeze the cluster forever.
- **Assumption:** non-Diver formations and asteroid roaming are unaffected; the seam is optional and only the Diver implements it.

# Problem statement

The audit runner's parent-first flow re-audits all children on every run because the freshness fingerprint includes the global git HEAD sha. In `--child-in-main-slot` mode, non-interactive runs leave all children with `partial` verdicts, which blocks the parent from recording a "Ready to close: Yes" result even when all parent ACs are met. This prevents audit completion for epics whose children were previously audited.

# Users

- **Audit runner / downtime worker** — expects a non-interactive audit of an epic to produce a valid verdict without requiring a live agent session.
- **Producer / human reviewer** — expects the audit to accurately reflect whether work is ready to close, not to block on stale or unserviced child verdicts.

# Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fingerprint scoping.** `_compute_content_fingerprint` no longer includes the global git HEAD sha as a sole invalidation trigger; instead it is scoped to child-relevant key files and/or commits so that unrelated HEAD movement on `dev` does not invalidate previously valid child audits.
- **AC2 — In-main-slot partial verdict handling.** When a child's `ac_results` remain `partial` because the invoking agent session never serviced the `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items, the parent audit treats those verdicts as "not assessed" (inherits the child's previously stored verdict or marks them reusable) rather than blocking the parent's readiness-to-close decision.
- **AC3 — Diagnostic clarity.** The audit output surfaces a clear, machine-parseable diagnostic that distinguishes a "child partial because unserviced in-main-slot" verdict from a genuine "not-ready" child verdict, including the reason code in the audit summary.
- **AC4 — No regression on interactive runs.** The above fixes do not change the behaviour of interactive audit runs (where an agent session *can* service in-main-slot items); those continue to honour the full in-main-slot workflow.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run the complete suite and confirm zero failures.

# Constraints

- The fix must not introduce a new mode flag or require operator configuration; it should be the default behaviour.
- The fix should be backward-compatible with persisted audit results (old fingerprint format should still be readable).
- The change scope is the audit runner's child freshness logic (`_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`), the in-main-slot verdict accumulation logic (`_build_issue_json`, `all_ac_acceptable`), and the diagnostic output path.

# Existing state

- `_compute_content_fingerprint` includes the current git HEAD sha — any new commit on `dev` invalidates every stored child audit.
- In `child_in_main_slot=True` mode, child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking session. In non-interactive runs, these are never serviced and stay `partial`.
- `_build_issue_json` includes child AC verdicts in `all_ac_acceptable`, so the parent is reported "Ready to close: No" even when all parent ACs are met.
- The runner's terminal lifecycle then demotes parent and children to `open`/`plan_complete` as a side effect.

# Desired change

1. **Scope the fingerprint**: Replace the global HEAD sha in `_compute_content_fingerprint` with a child-scoped hash (key files + relevant commits).
2. **Handle partial verdicts**: When computing `all_ac_acceptable`, skip children whose verdict is `partial` due to unserviced in-main-slot items — treat them as "not assessed" rather than "not accepted."
3. **Add diagnostics**: In the audit summary, emit a reason code or flag indicating when a child's `partial` verdict is due to unserviced in-main-slot items vs. genuine assessment failure.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audit/` or equivalent audit runner module — `_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`, `_build_issue_json`, in-main-slot verdict handling
- `scripts/audit_runner*` or equivalent — runner invocation, non-interactive path
- Audit output/summary formatter — diagnostic message generation

# Related work

- **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** — Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic (completed): the parent epic that discovered this issue during audit.
- **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** — Audit parent-first flow (internal assertion): the flow that triggers the re-audit on stale children.
- **SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE** — Audit in-main-slot mode (internal assertion): the mode that creates `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items.

# Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — fingerprint scoping is incomplete.** If child-relevant files/commits are not correctly identified, stale audits may still be invalidated or, conversely, genuinely stale audits may be reused. Mitigation: carefully identify the key files that each child audit covers; add a test case that simulates unrelated HEAD movement vs. child-relevant HEAD movement.
- **Risk — inheriting stale child verdicts masks real regressions.** If a child's code changed but the fingerprint didn't catch it, inheriting an old verdict is incorrect. Mitigation: the fingerprint scoping should cover all files relevant to the child audit.
- **Assumption:** all three suggested directions are desired (fingerprint scoping, partial-verdict handling, diagnostic clarity).
- **Assumption:** the audit runner is a Node.js/TypeScript or Python tool within the project; the fix applies to the runner's Python/TS source.

# Intake Brief: Review Queue depth notification is incorrect (AH-0MUDYTQ55002NUSJ)

## Headline

When the herdr worklist review queue is deep, the footer banner currently always
says "— audits will drain it". It must instead say "— focus on audits" while any
review item still lacks a current audit, and "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" once
every review item is audited.

## Problem statement

The herdr worklist shows a review-queue-depth banner when the root-only
`completed/in_review` count reaches `browseItemCount`. Today the banner copy is
fixed ("… — audits will drain it"), so it gives the same instruction whether
audits are still outstanding or the queue is fully audited and ready to ship.
The copy should reflect the actual audit state so the producer knows whether to
keep running audits or to ship.

## Users

- **Producer / sprint lead** — reads the banner to decide the next action.
  - *User story:* As a producer, when the review queue is deep and some items
    still need auditing, I want the banner to say "focus on audits" so I know
    audits are the drain. When every item in the queue has a current audit, I
    want the banner to say "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" so I know I can ship.
- **Downtime dispatcher / operator** — must be unaffected: the banner is
  display-only and never gates dispatch (WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the review queue is deep (root-only `completed/in_review` count ≥
   `browseItemCount`) **and** at least one root-level `in_review` item has an
   outstanding audit, the footer banner text reads exactly:
   `Review queue deep (<completed> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review) — focus on audits`.
2. When the review queue is deep **and** no root-level `in_review` item has an
   outstanding audit, the footer banner text reads exactly:
   `Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')`.
3. "Outstanding audit" is determined by the existing audit-freshness semantics
   (`isAuditFresh` / `inReviewBucket`): an `in_review` item with no stored
   `auditedAt`, or whose stored audit is not current, counts as outstanding. A
   fresh, passed audit does not.
4. The banner remains display-only: it never disables downtime dispatch, never
   writes/clears `.herdr-downtime-disabled`, and does not change code-freeze
   banner behaviour or the `showHelpText` gate.
5. Automated tests assert the exact rendered banner text for both variants and
   for the boundaries (deep+outstanding → deep+none; deep → shallow), using the
   existing worklist render test seams.
6. All related documentation/code comments describing the banner are updated to
   the new copy and the outstanding-audit condition.

## Constraints

- **Source repository:** the banner is implemented in the **ContextHub** repo
  (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`), not in `AI_Hell`. This work item is tracked
  in the `AI_Hell` worklog (consistent with existing tooling work items such as
  AH-0MUDYHPPC008F7PV); implementation must target the ContextHub source tree.
- `browseItemCount` default 20, re-read live from settings (no restart).
- Root-only counting via `wl list --status completed --stage in_review
  --root-only --json` (same query as `fetchCompletedItemCount`).
- No new persistence mechanism; reuse existing fetch helpers where possible.
- Display-only; must not reintroduce the sprint-complete auto-disable
  (WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD RCA root cause A).
- Keep the change minimal: banner copy + the state needed to choose it.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` renders the banner in the footer branch
  (~3596–3617): `const bannerText = \`Review queue deep${countDisplay} — audits will drain it\`;`
  where `countDisplay` = ` (<completed> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review)`.
- `refreshSprintState()` (~4531–4546) calls `fetchCompletedItemCount()`
  (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` ~684) and sets
  `sprintComplete = count >= liveBrowseCount`. Only a count is retained —
  per-item audit state is not currently available to the banner.
- `fetchCompletedItemCount()` runs `wl list --status completed --stage in_review
  --root-only --json` and returns the item count. `wl list --json` items expose
  `stage`, `status`, `auditedAt`, `auditResult`, `fingerprint`, `updatedAt`
  (but not `currentFingerprint`).
- Audit freshness is centralised: `isAuditFresh(...)` in
  `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` (~306) and the audit-aware bucket predicate
  `inReviewBucket(...)` in `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` (~360–389). The
  audit-dispatch tier uses the same predicate.
- There are currently **no automated tests** covering the banner text or
  `refreshSprintState` — this gap must be closed.

## Desired change

- Extend the banner-state refresh (or add a sibling helper) so it knows whether
  any root-level `in_review` item has an outstanding audit, in addition to the
  deep-queue boolean.
- Select the banner copy from that state:
  - outstanding audits → `Review queue deep (<n> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review) — focus on audits`;
  - none outstanding → `Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')`.
- Add regression tests for both variants and the transition boundaries.
- Update the code comments that describe the banner to match the new copy and
  condition.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — banner copy selection in the footer render
  branch (~3596–3617); `refreshSprintState` (~4531–4546); render-option plumbing
  for `sprintComplete` / `sprintCompletedCount` (~3359–3396, ~5893–5894).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchCompletedItemCount` (~681–699): extend
  or replace with an outstanding-audit-aware fetch of root `completed/in_review`
  items.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh` (~306) shared freshness
  predicate to reuse.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — `inReviewBucket` (~360–389) audit-aware
  predicate (alternative reuse).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — regression tests for both banner
  variants and boundaries.

## Related work

- **WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD** (ContextHub, done/deleted) — P2: replaced the
  sprint-complete auto-disable with the review policy; introduced the current
  "audits will drain it" banner copy.
- **WL-0MTHSHN5V008R5L0** (ContextHub, completed) — Auto-disable dispatching when
  sprint is complete; original sprint-complete banner ("Sprint Complete, hit S to
  ship").
- **WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG** (ContextHub, completed) — Allow `/skill:audit` on
  complete/in_review items without a valid audit; defines the "valid audit"
  (`isAuditFresh`) semantics reused here.
- **WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY** (ContextHub, completed) — Ship It shortcut ('S') with
  typed confirmation dispatching `/skill:ship release`.
- **WL-0MUDEJU9Z004UO2W** (ContextHub, blocked/plan_complete) — worklist
  pre-dialog ship gate + freeze-on-confirm integration (Ship Guard interaction).
- **WL-0MT2UQWOR007CYY9** (ContextHub, completed) — review-queue-depth gate for
  non-critical implement dispatch.
- **WL-0MU8808ZY0091JIA** (ContextHub, completed) — surface held gate in header
  (recent banner/header area change).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "outstanding audit" scope.** Defined as a **root-level**
  `in_review` item with no `auditedAt` or a non-current audit, matching the
  banner's root-only count. If child `in_review` items should also suppress the
  "Ready to Ship" copy, this must be confirmed (see Appendix).
- **Risk — fingerprint availability.** `wl list --json` does not return
  `currentFingerprint`, so `isAuditFresh` degrades to the 60 s time gate and a
  post-audit comment can falsely look stale, keeping "focus on audits" after
  audits complete. Mitigation: compute current fingerprints as the downtime
  worker/hydrator does, or add a purpose-built query.
- **Risk — misleading "Ready to Ship".** The 'S' ship shortcut is gated by the
  Ship Guard (live agent panes carrying this project's work-item IDs block
  shipping). "Ready to Ship" reflects audit state only; changing the guard is out
  of scope.
- **Assumption — condition structure preserved.** Only the deep-queue branch's
  copy changes; the banner still shows only when `isSprintComplete &&
  helpEnabled`.
- **Risk — missing test seams.** There is no existing banner test; the render
  pipeline is internal, so tests must use whatever seam the worklist suite
  already exercises, or expose a small pure helper for the copy decision.
- **Scope-creep risk:** do not touch the ship shortcut, Ship Guard, dispatch
  gating, or the queue-depth threshold. Capture extra opportunities as linked
  work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: What counts as an "outstanding audit"?**
  — Answer (research; no producer round): the freshness semantics already used
  across herdr — `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt, fingerprint,
  currentFingerprint)` returning false, or no stored `auditedAt`. Source:
  `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` (`isAuditFresh`), `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`
  (`inReviewBucket`), and the audit-dispatch tier in `downtime-worker.ts`.
  **ASSUMPTION — root-only scope chosen to match the existing banner count;
  confirm at plan if child `in_review` items should also count.**
- **Q: Where does the banner code live?**
  — Answer (research): the ContextHub repository

- **Q: Is 'S' the ship shortcut?**

  `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (`openShipItDialog`, `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`) and
  `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`.
- *Interview style:* no producer interview round was required — the seed

  confirmation.

# Leaderboard entry screen should show position in table

**Issue type:** feature · **Priority:** medium

> **Original request (preserved):** "When entering a high score into the
> leaderboard the leaderboard display the position of the players score in the
> leaderboard, filling in the initials as they are typed. Highlight that line
> somehow."

## Problem statement

On game over, a qualifying player types their three initials but receives no
feedback about where their score will land until they submit and return to the
menu. The ranked table on the game-over screen stays static, so the player
cannot tell whether the run is about to rank #1 or #10.

## Users

- An arcade player who has just finished a run and is entering their initials on
  the game-over screen.

  > **User story:** As a player entering my initials after a high score, I want
  > to see my score inserted into the leaderboard at the position it will take,
  > with my initials filling in live and my row highlighted, so that I know how
  > well I did before I commit.

## Existing state

- `GameOverScene` (`src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts`) renders a static leaderboard
  via `renderLeaderboard` (`src/ui/leaderboardView.ts`) and prompts for
  3-letter initials using the shared `FocusManager`.
- `src/core/Leaderboard.ts` owns persistence and ranking
  (`getEntries`, `addEntry`, `isQualifying`, `MAX_ENTRIES = 10`); `rank` is
  recomputed on read and never trusted from storage.
- Keystrokes currently update only the initials field text; the table is not
  re-rendered, and there is no marker for the player's prospective position.
- `LeaderboardScene` (main menu) renders the same table through the shared
  helper and must remain unchanged.

## Desired change

While a **qualifying** score is being entered on the game-over screen:

1. Compute the prospective entry's rank from the current table and the final
   score.
2. Show the player's row at that rank **immediately on screen open**, with
   initials rendered as placeholders until typing begins (Q2 answer:
   immediately).
3. Fill in the initials live as they are typed and update the row on every A–Z
   key and Backspace.
4. Highlight the player's row with a distinct colour plus a leading marker
   (Q1 answer: option A).
5. When the table already holds 10 entries, insert the prospective row at its
   true rank and drop the current lowest entry, so at most 10 rows are shown
   (Q3 answer: insert and drop).
6. On submit, the persisted entry occupies the same rank the preview showed.
7. Non-qualifying scores show no prospective row (explanatory message
   unchanged).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Live prospective row shown immediately:** For a qualifying score,
  the game-over leaderboard shows exactly one row representing the player's
  prospective entry as soon as the screen opens, at the rank it will occupy.
  The row's initials render as placeholders until typing begins.
- [ ] **AC2 — Live initials:** Each A–Z key press and Backspace updates that
  row's initials immediately (typed letters shown, unfilled slots rendered as
  placeholders), before any submit.
- [ ] **AC3 — Highlight:** The prospective row is visually distinguishable from
  every other row by a distinct colour plus a leading marker (e.g. `▶`).
- [ ] **AC4 — Correct placement and cap:** The prospective row is inserted by
  score descending with the same stable tie-break as `Leaderboard.addEntry`;
  the table never shows more than `MAX_ENTRIES` (10) rows, and when full the
  current lowest entry is displaced.
- [ ] **AC5 — Qualifying only:** Non-qualifying scores render no prospective
  row and write nothing to storage.
- [ ] **AC6 — Submit consistency:** After submit, the persisted entry occupies
  the same rank shown by the preview.
- [ ] **AC7 — Regression:** `LeaderboardScene` (main-menu table) is unchanged
  and existing GameOverScene/Leaderboard tests continue to pass.
- [ ] **AC8 — Testing/validation:** New unit tests cover rank insertion
  (including equal-score ties and full-table displacement), immediate preview
  visibility before typing, live initials update, highlight marker/colour,
  Backspace-to-empty, and non-qualifying behaviour.
- [ ] **AC9 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect
  the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
  site entries.
- [ ] **AC10 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Keyboard-only entry through `FocusManager` is retained; no on-screen
  keyboard is added.
- Reuse `src/ui/leaderboardView.ts` for rendering where practical so the
  game-over and main-menu tables stay consistent.
- `Leaderboard.ts` remains the single owner of ranking and persistence; a pure,
  testable helper for the prospective rank is preferred over duplicating sort
  logic in the scene.
- No new dependencies.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the prospective rank uses the same stable tie-break as
  `addEntry` — a new equal score ranks after existing equal-score entries.
- **Assumption:** the prospective row's date column shows today's ISO date
  (`todayISO()`), matching the eventual persisted entry.
- **Assumption:** highlighting applies only to the game-over entry screen; the
  main-menu `LeaderboardScene` table is unchanged.
- **Risk (scope creep):** extra polish (animation, sound, online leaderboard)
  is recorded as separate linked work items, not added to this scope.
- **Risk:** re-rendering rows on each keystroke could leak text objects; the
  implementation should destroy/replace preview rows rather than accumulate
  them.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/Leaderboard.ts` — add a pure helper to compute the prospective
  ranked preview (reusing the existing `sortAndRank` semantics).
- `src/ui/leaderboardView.ts` — support a highlighted/preview row in
  `renderLeaderboard` (or a sibling helper).
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` — render and refresh the prospective row on
  initials changes.
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.test.ts` — tests for the preview behaviour.
- `src/ui/leaderboardView.test.ts` (new if no existing coverage) — tests for
  highlighted/preview row formatting.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §5 — document the live preview-row UX.
- `README.md` §Leaderboard — update the game-over description.

- **Implement game-over qualifying, date and full leaderboard (AH-0MUD9ZOM4001LACR)**

- **Test: Game-over leaderboard UX (AH-0MUD9ZNN30065ZLP)** (completed) —

  initials-entry focus model reused here.
- **Implement GameOverScene — scoring, lives, game-over flow
  (AH-0MU731426003FE71)** (completed) — scene this feature modifies.
- **Implement Leaderboard persistence module (AH-0MUD9ZOAR0099DJZ)** (completed)
  — ranking API used for placement.
- **Docs: GDD and README leaderboard updates (AH-0MUD9ZP94006OYL4)**

- `README.md` — matched: ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance, add (+265 more)

- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: ac1, ac4, add, added, animation (+201 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Highlight treatment.** How should the player's prospective row be
  highlighted? Options: A) distinct colour plus a leading marker (e.g. `▶`);
  B) blinking/pulsing row; C) background panel behind the row; D) other.
  **Recommended:** A. — **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "A".

  visible immediately when a qualifying game-over screen opens (initials shown

  **Recommended:** visible immediately. — **Answer (producer, interactive

- **Q3 — Full-table behaviour.** When the table already holds 10 entries and
  the score qualifies, should the preview insert at its true rank and drop the

  **Recommended:** drop the lowest. — **Answer (producer, interactive reply):**

- [ ] **AC5** — Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick, verified with multiple active weapons.

# Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign

## Problem statement

**Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation (AH-0MUH6LEYY0054E63)** makes the campaign all-or-nothing: with `sequencedWavesEnabled` off every level uses the hand-authored static `LEVELS`, and with it on *every* level is generated from the difficulty-curve config. A designer cannot hand-tune the levels that matter (onboarding, boss lead-in, a specific set-piece) while letting the sequencer ramp the rest. This item lets a single campaign **mix** generated and scripted levels, per level.

## Users

- As a **designer**, I want to mark individual levels as generated or scripted, so I can hand-tune onboarding and set-piece levels while the sequencer handles the rest.
- As a **player**, I want the campaign to keep its hand-authored early levels but ramp difficulty in later levels, so each run is both learnable and challenging.
- As a **maintainer**, I want a single, data-driven campaign definition whose generated and scripted sources are explicit and testable, so the two paths cannot silently diverge.

## Existing state

- **Campaign builder** — `buildSequencedLevels(rows?, candidates?)` in `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` groups `DifficultyCurveRow[]` by level, calls the read-only `sequencer()` once per generated level with `defaultShootEnabled = level >= FIRST_FIRING_LEVEL (4)`, converts `ShootableWave.groups` to `WaveGroup`s and returns `LevelDefinition[]`. On empty/degenerate input or a sequencer throw it returns static `LEVELS` (whole-campaign fallback). It has **no notion of a per-level source**.
- **Config** — `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` is one row per `(level, wave)` with columns `level,levelName,wave,targetDifficulty`; loaded by `loadDifficultyCurves()` (`src/core/configStore.ts`) through the CSV pipeline (dev `/api/csv/...`, bundled `?raw` in production) with `defaultDifficultyCurves()` computed from the static `LEVELS` calibration as the fallback. Types live in `src/core/configTypes.ts` (`DifficultyCurveRow`); codec/validator in `src/core/csv.ts` (`parseDifficultyCurves` / `serializeDifficultyCurves` / `validateDifficultyCurveRow`).
- **Static campaign** — `LEVELS` in `src/waves/Formations.ts`: five `LevelDefinition`s (names, waves, `shootEnabled`). Levels 1–3 do not fire; 4–5 do (GDD §2.4/§2.5).
- **Wiring** — `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` is being wired (in-progress child **Opt-in toggle and PlayScene wiring (AH-0MUITS1SM008GPR9)**) to read the opt-in `sequencedWavesEnabled` toggle and, when on, call `buildSequencedLevels()` and inject the result via `WaveManager.setLevels()`. `WaveManager` already accepts injected `LevelDefinition[]` and defaults to `LEVELS`.

## Desired change

Extend the campaign builder so each level's source is selectable, and merge the two sources into one `LevelDefinition[]`:

- A level marked **`generated`** is produced by `sequencer()` from that level's curve rows (as today, with `shootEnabled` from the level's fire rule).
- A level marked **`scripted`** is taken **byte-for-byte from static `LEVELS`** (its own waves and its own `shootEnabled`), and is not passed to the sequencer.
- The campaign skeleton, the config representation of the selector, and the fallback scope are the three decisions in **Open questions** below; the proposed answers are the recommended options there.

When `sequencedWavesEnabled` is **off**, behaviour is unchanged: static `LEVELS` exactly. Mixed mode is only reachable with the toggle on.

## Acceptance criteria (draft — pending Open questions)

- **Per-level source selection** — a campaign can be configured with a mix of generated and scripted levels; `buildSequencedLevels()` returns the correct source per level (test asserts a mixed config yields scripted levels identical to the matching `LEVELS` entries and generated levels differing from static `LEVELS`).
- **Scripted levels are exact** — every scripted level's `LevelDefinition` (name, wave count, groups, spacing, positions and `shootEnabled`) is deeply equal to the corresponding static `LEVELS` definition (byte-for-byte in intent; test asserts deep equality).
- **Generated levels unchanged** — a generated level in a mixed campaign is identical to the same level built by today's all-generated builder for the same curve and candidate pool (determinism preserved; no RNG/clock/I-O).
- **Fire rule respected per source** — generated levels 1–3 have `shootEnabled=false` and 4+ `true`; scripted levels keep `LEVELS`' own flags (test asserts both).
- **Fallback is safe** — a missing/empty/malformed curve for a generated level, or an empty candidate pool, never produces an unplayable campaign: the affected level (or campaign, per the Open question decision) falls back to static `LEVELS` and the game does not crash (test covers each case).
- **Runtime wiring** — with the toggle on and a mixed config, `PlayScene` runs the mixed campaign via `WaveManager`; with the toggle off it runs static `LEVELS` exactly (test asserts both paths at the scene seam).
- **Testing/validation** — new/updated unit and integration tests cover the selector parsing, mixed merge, scripted deep-equality, generated equivalence, fire rule and fallback, and they are meaningful and passing.
- **Documentation** — all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the README, `docs/Game Design Document.md` and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
- **No regressions** — the full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`).

## Constraints

- **Pure core stays pure** — `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` must not be modified (read-only call site).
- **Determinism** — generation remains a pure function of config + candidate pool; scripted levels are static data.
- **No behavioural change when the toggle is off** — existing `WaveManager`/`PlayScene`/campaign tests pass unchanged.
- **CSV pipeline is the source of truth** — any new config goes through the existing codec/`configStore`/Vite plugin pattern; malformed rows must not crash.
- **Backwards compatibility** — the existing 4-column `difficulty-curves.csv` and `defaultDifficultyCurves()` must keep working; existing tests pass unchanged.
- UK English in prose; Markdown in the work item.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — add per-level source selection and the scripted/generated merge; keep the fallback guard.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` — mixed-campaign tests (source selection, scripted deep-equality, generated equivalence, fallback).
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — extend `DifficultyCurveRow` with the source field (if the explicit-selector option is chosen).
- `src/core/csv.ts` — extend the difficulty-curve codec/validator for the source field.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — add the per-level source column/rows (if the explicit-selector option is chosen).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — keep `loadDifficultyCurves()` / `defaultDifficultyCurves()` consistent with the selector.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static `LEVELS` referenced as the scripted source (read-only).
- `src/core/rules.ts` — `sequencedWavesEnabled` toggle (existing; only a settings-store selector option would change it).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — already injects the built campaign; verify mixed campaigns flow through unchanged.
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — whitelist/validation if the CSV schema changes.
- Test files: `src/core/csv.test.ts`, `src/core/configStore.test.ts`, `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§2.4/§2.5), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§9 sequencer), `README.md`.

## Related work

- **Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation (AH-0MUH6LEYY0054E63)** — the opt-in wiring this builds on; defers mixed campaigns to this item.
- **Implement runtime auto-sequencer for dynamic difficulty adjustment (AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X)** — delivered `sequencer()`.
- **Campaign builder: config to generated level definitions (AH-0MUITS0VD000DVSV)** — delivered `buildSequencedLevels()` (completed).
- **Difficulty-curve config, codec and CSV loader (AH-0MUITRZZE000OYQE)** — delivered the CSV schema/codec this item may extend (completed).
- **Opt-in toggle and PlayScene wiring (AH-0MUITS1SM008GPR9)** — the wiring this depends on (in-progress).
- **Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL)** — designer tool for curves; out of scope here.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §2.4/§2.5 fire rules, §3.2 level themes.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §9 enemy difficulty scoring / sequencer.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Config-schema churn** — an explicit `source` column changes `DifficultyCurveRow`, the codec and the CSV that a just-completed child defined; mitigated by making the field default to `generated` so existing rows/tests are unaffected (if that option is chosen).
- **Fallback scope** — a whole-campaign fallback on one bad generated level would silently discard a designer's other scripted/generated choices; the recommended per-level fallback avoids this (see Open questions).
- **Scripted numbering** — a level marked scripted whose number has no `LEVELS` entry is undefined; must be handled explicitly (fallback or reject) rather than crashing.
- **Scope creep** — runtime curve editing (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL) and any sequencer-algorithm change are out of scope; extra opportunities are recorded as linked work items.
- **Assumption (toggle interaction)** — mixed mode is only active when `sequencedWavesEnabled` is on; when off, static `LEVELS` is used unchanged.
- **Assumption (scripted source is `LEVELS`)** — scripted levels are referenced by level number into static `LEVELS`; no new hand-authored wave data is introduced.

## Open questions (producer review required)

1. **How should the per-level source selector be declared?** Options: (a) explicit `source` column in `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` (`generated`|`scripted`); (b) presence/absence of curve rows (a level with no rows is scripted); (c) a separate settings-store or CSV selector (e.g. `GameRules.scriptedLevels: number[]`). **Recommended: (a)** — explicit and colocated with the curve, matching "mark individual levels"; requires `targetDifficulty` to be optional for scripted rows. This is a schema change to `DifficultyCurveRow`/codec/CSV.
2. **What determines the campaign skeleton and ordering when mixing?** Options: (a) start from all static `LEVELS`, override the configured levels per their source, and append generated levels numbered beyond `LEVEL_COUNT`; (b) the campaign is exactly the configured levels, with scripted ones referencing `LEVELS` by number; (c) all static levels are scripted by default and only configured levels are generated. **Recommended: (a)** — preserves the shipped five-level campaign and guarantees onboarding levels exist.
3. **What is the fallback scope when a generated level has no usable curve?** Options: (a) per-level — use that level's static `LEVELS` definition if one exists, otherwise skip/apply a safe guard; (b) whole-campaign — fall back to all of static `LEVELS` (current builder behaviour); (c) per-level for a bad level, whole-campaign only when the entire config is empty. **Recommended: (a)** — one bad level must not discard the rest of a mixed campaign.

# Intake brief — Harvester enemy

**Headline:** Add a Harvester enemy archetype — a large, slow, roaming enemy
that actively seeks and absorbs the nearest mineral and survives five player
bullets — plus the shared multi-hit health support and mineral-seeker seam it
needs in both the shipped game and the enemy gym.

## Problem statement

The bestiary currently has no enemy that competes with the player for
minerals. Non-asteroid enemies already absorb any mineral they happen to
overlap (GDD §4.4.1), but none deliberately hunts the field. The Harvester
introduces a mineral-denial threat: it actively drives to the nearest mineral,
is large (easy to hit and quick to absorb), slow to cross the screen, and
durable (five hits), forcing the player to spend ammunition and attention on it
before it strips the field.

## Users

- **As a player**, I want a durable enemy that actively steals minerals, so
  that collecting minerals becomes a contest rather than a free pickup.
- **As a player**, I want the Harvester to be large and slow, so that the
  five-hit cost is fair and readable rather than punishing.
- **As a designer**, I want to tune the Harvester (size, colour, speed,
  health, score) through the existing CSV/enemy-config pipeline without
  touching scene code.
- **As a developer**, I want multi-hit health and mineral seeking to be shared,
  data-driven capabilities, so future multi-hit or seeking enemies are cheap
  and the game and gyms cannot diverge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — New `harvester` archetype is registered and discoverable.** A
  `harvester` row exists in `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` with a matching seed
  fallback in `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, is mapped in
  `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`, appears in the gym index, and spawns/renders
  in `GymEnemies`. Verified by config/CSV tests and a gym spawn test.
- [ ] **AC2 — Mineral-seeking behaviour.** The Harvester moves toward the
  nearest live mineral at its configured (slow) speed and absorbs it on
  overlap using the existing enemy-absorption rule, incrementing its tracked
  mineral count. When no mineral exists it holds station / continues its idle
  drift (per Q2). Verified by deterministic entity + scene tests that place
  minerals and assert the Harvester closes distance and consumes them.
- [ ] **AC3 — Five-hit destruction.** The Harvester survives exactly five
  player-bullet hits. Each non-lethal hit consumes the bullet and produces
  readable feedback; the fifth hit destroys it, plays destruction audio/VFX
  exactly once, awards its score, advances wave accounting, and re-drops
  25–50 % of absorbed minerals per the existing rule. Verified by a
  five-hit test and a single-destruction/single-audio regression test.
- [ ] **AC4 — Existing enemies are unchanged.** All current 1-HP enemies
  (Scout, Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm, Asteroid) remain destroyed by one hit and
  their tests stay green.
- [ ] **AC5 — Game ↔ gym parity.** The Harvester's seek, absorption and
  five-hit destruction run through the same shared code path in `PlayScene` and
  in `GymEnemies` (per the gym-parity principle); no scene re-implements the
  behaviour.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation.** New unit/integration tests cover: config
  codec round-trip (including any new health column), factory mapping, seek
  target selection (nearest mineral; none present), absorption counting,
  five-hit destruction, and a `PlayScene` + `GymEnemies` parity check. Full
  project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
  the changes, including the Game Design Document enemy catalog / health model
  (§2.3, §4.1, §4.4.1, §6.5), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  (§1/§8 enemy catalog and add-an-enemy checklist), the README enemy list, and
  code comments.

## Constraints

- **Data-driven:** tuning lives in the CSV/enemy-config pipeline; no new
  per-enemy scene or hard-coded archetype branch.
- **Single source of truth:** no duplication of collision, mineral-collection,
  or health logic — this is a hard requirement of the gym-parity epic
  (`AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`).
- **No regression:** existing 1-HP enemies and their tests must be untouched
  semantically.
- **Surgical:** match existing entity/config/scene style; do not delete
  unrelated dead code (report it instead).
- **UK English** in all written output and documentation.
- **Gating:** implementation proceeds only through `/skill:implement`; this
  intake does not authorise code changes.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-27 against HEAD)

- Enemy archetypes are **data, not code**: `EnemyConfig` (`src/core/configTypes.ts`),
  one CSV row per archetype (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`), seed fallbacks in
  `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, factory mapping in `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`.
- All regular enemies are **1 HP** (destroyed by a single bullet) and the GDD
  states this explicitly (`docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.3, §4.1, §6.5).
  Only the Boss is multi-hit (4-phase). There is an optional `takeDamage?()`
  seam on entities (`CombatCoreScene`, `CombatScene`, `GymFormationScene`), but
  the shared generic path currently calls it **without** running
  `onEnemyDestroyed()`/destruction audio when the entity finally dies — that
  is a gap this work must close for a multi-hit regular enemy to score, drop
  minerals and advance waves correctly.
- The Asteroid is the precedent for a **non-formation roamer**: it has
  `formationKind: single`, overrides `updatePosition(dt)` (called by the gym
  and game before `applyFormationPosition`) and `applyFormationPosition` is a
  no-op.
- Minerals already exist: `Mineral` (`src/entities/Mineral.ts`), collection and
  non-asteroid absorption in `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`
  (`collectMinerals`), kill re-drop in `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts`,
  and the 25–50 % re-drop fraction in `src/core/rules.ts`. `BaseEnemy` already
  tracks `mineralCount` / `collectMineral()` / `mineralRedropCount()`.
- The shared enemy-fire dispatcher (`src/entities/enemyFire.ts`) already
  mentions the "planned Harvester" as the example of a one-line wiring change.

## Desired change

1. Generalise enemy health data-driven (pending Q1) so a regular enemy can
   require N hits, and make the shared collision path correctly finalise a
   multi-hit kill (audio, `onEnemyDestroyed`, drops, wave accounting).
2. Add a `Harvester` entity that roams (like the Asteroid) and steers toward
   the nearest live mineral, absorbing it on overlap.
3. Register the archetype (CSV + seed + factory + score) and expose it in the
   gym.
4. Integrate it into the campaign per Q3 (roadmap: available in the gym and as
   a rare roaming spawn in later levels).
5. Update the GDD/ENEMY design docs/README for the health-model and enemy
   catalog changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — New `harvester` row; add a `health` column if
  Q1 is answered "data-driven".
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — `health` field on `EnemyConfig` (if data-driven).
- `src/core/csv.ts` — `health` column in `ENEMY_COLUMN_ORDER`, coercion and
  validation.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — `harvester` seed fallback (+ default health).
- `src/entities/Harvester.ts` — New roamer entity: slow seek movement, large
  body, multi-hit health, no firing.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — Shared multi-hit health / `takeDamage`
  behaviour (or a small shared health helper).
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — Map `harvester` → `Harvester`.
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` — No-firing archetype handling (existing fallback
  to aimed fire must be avoided for the Harvester).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — Finalise a multi-hit kill through
  `onEnemyDestroyed` + destruction audio; supply the live mineral field to
  seeking entities.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Wire seeking/minerals, score value, roamer
  movement, wave/score accounting.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` + `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` —
  Expose the same mineral list/seek seam and multi-hit path.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` / `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` /
  `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — Campaign spawn integration per Q3.
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — Optional `health` difficulty factor
  (recommended follow-up, not necessarily in scope).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`,
  `README.md` — Documentation updates.
- Tests: `src/entities/Harvester.test.ts`,
  `src/entities/enemyFactory.test.ts`, `src/core/csv.test.ts`,
  `src/core/enemyConfig.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.

## Related work

- `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` — Gym↔game behavioural-parity epic (critical, open).
  This work must consume the shared cores it establishes and must not add a new
  divergence.
- `AH-0MUII3BBW000XZ46` — Shared enemy-fire dispatch (completed). Names the
  Harvester as the exemplar of one-line fire wiring.
- `AH-0MUII3DHM008L7JF` — Shared mineral layer: collection, hold/overflow,
  choice overlay (completed).
- `AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB` — Gym asteroids do not drop minerals / shared
  kill-drop rule (open); relevant to the re-drop path.
- `AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F` — E6 Asteroid non-formation roamer (completed).
  Precedent architecture for a roaming enemy.
- `AH-0MT7V5UH90023XWR` — Clarify enemy health / one-hit destruction model in
  GDD (completed). The GDD currently pins regular enemies at 1 HP; a 5-HP
  regular enemy requires an explicit, documented revision (see Q1).
- `AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K` — Enemy difficulty scoring (completed). Health is not
  currently a scored factor (see Risks).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — health-model conflict.** A 5-HP regular enemy contradicts the GDD's
  explicit "all regular enemies (E1–E5) are 1 HP" and "no multi-hit bullet"
  rules. Mitigation: settle Q1 before implementation and update the GDD.
- **Risk — multi-hit kill does not finalise.** The current
  `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` `takeDamage` branch skips `onEnemyDestroyed` and
  destruction audio. Mitigation: extend the shared seam and pin it with a test
  so score/wave/drop/audio happen exactly once on the killing blow.
- **Risk — seek seam duplication.** Giving the entity the mineral list must be
  done once in the shared collision/tick path, not copied into each scene
  (parity epic). Mitigation: add a single `setSeekTargets`/equivalent seam
  alongside the existing `setAimTarget`.
- **Risk — difficulty under-scoring.** `enemyDifficulty` has no health factor,
  so a 5-HP enemy may score lower than its true threat. Mitigation: record a
  linked follow-up work item; do not let it block this feature.
- **Risk — scope creep into wave/level design.** Wiring a new roamer into the
  campaign can balloon. Mitigation: Q3 fixes scope up front; keep the gym
  demonstration as the minimum and a rare campaign spawn as the target.
- **Assumption — "collects it" reuses existing absorption.** The Harvester
  absorbs the mineral on overlap and tallies it; on death it re-drops 25–50 %
  per the existing rule. (Confirm via Q2.)
- **Assumption — tuning values are implementation/gym choices.** "Large" and
  "slow" are the requirements; exact px size/speed/colour are chosen and tuned
  in the gym (indicative: size ≈ 40–48 px, speed ≈ 20–30 px/s).
- **Assumption — the Harvester does not fire** unless Q2 says otherwise.

## Open questions (routed to the producer)

These are recorded as a comment and repeated here; the item is flagged
`needs-producer-review`.

1. **Health model (blocking).** A 5-HP regular enemy breaks the GDD's explicit
   1-HP model. Options: (a) generalise health data-driven (new `health` CSV
   column + GDD update; P4 Bomb still deals no damage); (b) keep a
   Harvester-only code constant; (c) something else. **Recommended:** (a) — it
   is the smallest durable change, serves future multi-hit enemies, and keeps
   tuning in the CSV. Sub-question: should each non-lethal hit show a health
   indicator (e.g. colour/scale change), or is ordinary hit feedback enough?
2. **Mineral-seeking semantics (blocking).** Options: (a) always seek the
   nearest live mineral anywhere on the field; absorb on overlap; no firing;
   cannot steal from the player's hold; re-drop per the existing 25–50 % rule.
   (b) only seek minerals within a detection radius. (c) also fire at the
   player. **Recommended:** (a) — it matches "moves towards the nearest
   mineral" literally and reuses the whole existing mineral layer.
3. **Spawn / campaign integration (blocking).** Options: (a) available in the
   gym **and** added to the campaign as a rare roaming spawn in later levels;
   (b) gym-only archetype for now; (c) a fixed formation group. **Recommended:**
   (a) — it makes the enemy playable in the campaign and visible in the gym,
   which is where tuning happens.
4. *(Non-blocking)* Score value and difficulty weight. **Recommended:** score
   ≈ 400 (durable, between Tank 300 and Boss phases) and a linked follow-up to
   add a `health` factor to `enemyDifficulty`, rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix — clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (health model) — **OPEN QUESTION**; awaiting producer answer. Options and
  recommendation recorded above (recommended: data-driven `health` column +
  GDD update; P4 Bomb unchanged).
- Q2 (mineral-seeking semantics) — **OPEN QUESTION**; awaiting producer answer
  (recommended: seek nearest live mineral anywhere; no firing; existing absorb
  and re-drop; no hold theft).
- Q3 (spawn / campaign integration) — **OPEN QUESTION**; awaiting producer
  answer (recommended: gym + rare campaign roaming spawn in later levels).
- Q4 (score/difficulty) — **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking)**; awaiting producer
  answer (recommended: score ≈ 400; difficulty health factor as a follow-up).
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Is the Harvester already tracked or
  referenced?" — Research: `wl search harvester` and repo grep. Result: only
  this item and a code comment in `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` naming the
  "planned Harvester"; `src/entities/enemyFire.test.ts` uses `'harvester'` as
  a fallback-key example. No duplicate work item exists.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Does multi-hit support already exist for
  regular enemies?" — Research: inspected `CombatScene.onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`,
  `GymFormationScene` `FormationSceneEntity.takeDamage`, and `Boss.takeDamage`.
  Result: an optional `takeDamage` seam exists, but the shared generic path
  does not finalise a kill (`onEnemyDestroyed`/destruction audio) — a gap to
  close (see Risks).
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "How do minerals and roaming enemies
  currently work?" — Research: read `mineralLayer.ts`, `Mineral.ts`,
  `mineralKillDrops.ts`, `BaseEnemy` mineral accounting, and `Asteroid.ts`.
  Result: absorption + re-drop and the non-formation roamer pattern both exist
  and are reusable; the only new capability is *seeking* the nearest mineral.
